summary.en: Security forces in Kurram repelled a cross‑border infiltration, killing a Pakistani soldier and twelve militants, including Afghan Taliban fighters. The Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed twelve civilians, prompting a Saudi‑led coalition vow of a decisive response. Afghanistan announced a potential China‑to‑Persian Gulf trade corridor, linking regional commerce to the security environment. Traders in Panjgur observed a strike, indicating domestic economic unrest. The conflict remains deadly, with 1,794 battle‑related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Kurram avverget en grenseoverskridende infiltrasjon, og drepte en pakistansk soldat og tolv militante, inkludert afghanske Taliban‑krigere. Houthi‑angrepet på Riyadhs King Khalid internasjonale flyplass drepte tolv sivile, og førte til at den saudisk‑ledede koalisjonen lovet en avgjørende respons. Afghanistan kunngjorde en potensiell handelskoridor fra Kina til Persiabukta, som knytter regional handel til sikkerhetsmiljøet. Handlere i Panjgur observerte et streik, noe som indikerer innenlandsk økonomisk uro. Konflikten forblir dødelig, med 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
